checked_claims.note: Imported clause (AJ a P2-bundle; U smooth surjective of pure relative dimension two; Z canonically Ord(U)). Not verifiable from the dependency artifacts, which are unreachable in this workspace (repo/ is a dangling symlink), but each component is independently corroborated at packet level: FND-0139 and FND-0142 give h^0(L)=3 identically on the balanced+(N) locus (B_4 empty because the only Clifford-equality case is the hyperelliptic-composed pencil, which FND-0125 shows has F=O(2)+O(7)); FND-0107 supplies the correct AJ model and its agreement with Proj(pi_*L) exactly where h^0 is constant; FND-0134 gives nonemptiness and fibrewise density of the reduced-support open; FND-0064 and FND-0141 give the finite etale S_6-ordering torsor and S-smoothness of relative dimension two over a reduced base. S normal implies S reduced, so the Grauert-based reduced-base restriction recorded by REV-0116 and REV-0142 is satisfied. Checked also that W_5 is taken as the canonical degree-sixteen HN quotient rather than a split summand, i.e. the filtered form required by FND-0097, whose exactness inputs hold at (6,6) by the degree bounds of FND-0099 (deg W_4=20>10, deg W_4(-Gamma)=14>10).

S normal Noetherian implies each connected component S_alpha is open, closed, normal and integral. AJ_alpha is normal because Zariski-locally it is P^2 over a normal domain and polynomial extensions/localizations of normal domains are normal; it is connected as a Zariski-locally trivial fibration with connected fibres over a connected base, and normal plus connected plus locally Noetherian gives integral. U_alpha is a nonempty open (nonemptiness from fibrewise density, FND-0134) of an integral normal scheme, hence integral and normal, and dense, so dim U_alpha = dim AJ_alpha = dim S_alpha + 2 for a finite-type k-scheme. Minor presentational compression, not a defect: the attempt's phrase 'Zariski-locally it is P2 times an integral scheme' establishes local integrality only; global integrality needs the connectedness step just given, which is immediate.

Re-derived independently. U_alpha is connected, locally Noetherian and finite type over k, so finite etale covers correspond to finite pi_1^et-sets and connected components to orbits. For a right S_6-torsor, trivializing one geometric fibre by a chosen ordering makes monodromy commute with the right action, hence act by left multiplication through rho_alpha; orbits of left multiplication by H_alpha are the sets H_alpha g, whose number is [S_6:H_alpha]. Z_alpha is etale over the normal U_alpha, hence normal; a locally Noetherian normal scheme is locally integral, so its irreducible components are its connected components. This is exactly the normality hypothesis flagged as load-bearing by FND-0132, and it is retained here rather than assumed away. k algebraically closed makes the arithmetic/geometric monodromy distinction of FND-0148 vacuous.

Each orbit H_alpha g has cardinality |H_alpha|, so each component has degree |H_alpha| over the connected U_alpha; a finite etale map is open and closed, so the image of a component is open and closed in the connected U_alpha, hence all of it (surjectivity). Finite surjective maps preserve dimension, giving dim = dim U_alpha = dim S_alpha + 2. Right multiplication is transitive on {H_alpha g} and the stabilizer of H_alpha g is g^{-1}H_alpha g, conjugate to H_alpha, so the transitivity and stabilizer clauses hold and Z_alpha is irreducible iff [S_6:H_alpha]=1 iff H_alpha=S_6. See finding candidate FC-REV0150-COSET-SIDE for a nomenclature hazard in the phrase 'left cosets' that does not affect the truth of the clause.

Re-derived. At a geometric point of Z the incidence gives O_C(Gamma) = L exactly (the relative-equivalence twist of FND-0133 is trivial on a point), and weak (N) gives L = omega_C(-D) by the degree argument of FND-0105 (deg A = 0), so O_C(D) = omega_C(-Gamma) of degree 4. By FND-0142, h^0(O_C(D)) = 2 on every balanced+(N) fibre, and gamma^* is injective on H^0(P^1,O(1)), so gamma^*H^0(O(1)) is a two-dimensional subspace of a two-dimensional space: the pencil is complete and base-point-free, and gamma is the morphism it defines. Any a fixing every x_i fixes Gamma as a divisor and preserves omega_C, hence preserves omega_C(-Gamma), permutes the members of the complete pencil, and induces b in PGL_2 with b o gamma = gamma o a; b is unique because gamma is surjective, giving injectivity. Direction of the argument matters and is correct here: it starts from Aut(C;x_1,...,x_6), the group relevant to a forgetful map, rather than from Aut(C,gamma,Gamma), which is precisely the failure mode warned about in FND-0137; it is consistent with the functorial reconstruction recorded in FND-0147. The scope disclaimer that this is objectwise and not a full-faithfulness statement is accurate.

finding_candidates.statement: The FND-0137 obstruction — that a rigidity argument passing through an induced PGL_2 transformation proves the clause only for Aut(C,gamma,Gamma) and not for the group Aut(C,Gamma) relevant to a forgetful map — is discharged by exactly one numerical condition, namely completeness of the residual pencil h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) = h^0(O_C(D)) = 2. Mechanism: an automorphism a fixing the six labelled points fixes Gamma and preserves omega_C, hence preserves omega_C(-Gamma); when h^0 = 2 the pulled-back pencil gamma^*H^0(P^1,O(1)) exhausts H^0(omega_C(-Gamma)), so gamma IS the complete-pencil morphism and a permutes its members, producing the target automorphism b, unique by surjectivity of gamma. The condition is not cosmetic: on any stratum with h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 3 the pulled-back pencil is a proper subpencil of a net, preservation of omega_C(-Gamma) no longer forces preservation of gamma, and surjectivity of the forgetful homomorphism can genuinely fail. Consequently any downstream artifact citing an inertia or stabilizer isomorphism of this shape must certify h^0 = 2 pointwise on its whole base (at (6,6) this is supplied by fibrewise balancedness via FND-0142 plus FND-0125, and requires (N) via FND-0105 to identify L with omega_C(-D) in the first place), and must not import the clause onto unbalanced, merely generically balanced, or closure strata.

finding_candidates.statement: In the component formula for a RIGHT S_6-torsor, the index set H\S_6 must be read as the set of orbits of left multiplication by H, i.e. the sets Hg, which under standard nomenclature are right cosets; the phrase 'left cosets H\S_6' used both in ATT-0101's theorem statement and in the wording of FND-0148 is a mislabel of the correct object. The distinction is typing-critical rather than cosmetic downstream: the right deck action descends to {Hg} (Hg . g' = Hgg', transitive, stabilizer of Hg equal to g^{-1}Hg), whereas on the genuine left-coset set S_6/H = {gH} right multiplication is not well defined at all, so any artifact that writes gH and then applies the deck action, or that computes a stabilizer as gHg^{-1} on that indexing, is ill-typed and will produce the wrong conjugacy bookkeeping. Recommended discipline for downstream C66-GEO-COMP and C66-TATE-* artifacts: write 'the orbit set H\S_6 of left multiplication' and record the stabilizer as g^{-1}Hg.

finding_candidates.statement: A corollary of the confirmed component classification, verified here and not recorded in the packet: because the right S_6-action is transitive on the components of Z_alpha with stabilizer conjugate to H_alpha, all components are isomorphic as U_alpha-schemes, and for any additive S_6-equivariant invariant — in particular H^*(-;Q) and H^{BM}_*(-;Q) with their mixed Hodge structures — one has H^*(Z_alpha;Q) = Ind_{H_alpha}^{S_6} H^*(Z_alpha^1;Q), where Z_alpha^1 is the component with stabilizer H_alpha, and the H_alpha-action on H^*(Z_alpha^1) is by the residual deck transformations. Consistency check: taking S_6-invariants returns H^*(Z_alpha^1;Q)^{H_alpha} = H^*(U_alpha;Q), as it must. Two consequences for the downstream nodes. (i) The entire S_6-isotypic structure of the ordered failure locus is determined by the single subgroup H_alpha together with the H_alpha-representation on one component, so the uncomputed H_alpha of GAP-COMP-MONODROMY is the only obstruction to an exact equivariant decomposition — the component count alone is not additional information. (ii) This is a purely formal induction statement and upgrades nothing to Tate: it is fully compatible with H^*(Z_alpha^1) carrying non-Tate summands, which is precisely the hazard recorded in FND-0053, and it is stated with Q-coefficients on schemes, so it carries none of the integral-coefficient or coarse-space content excluded by FND-0075.

strongest_attack: The strongest available attack is on the final stabilizer clause, and it fails only because of a hypothesis the artifact actually carries. The clause asserts that every a in Aut(C;x_1,...,x_6) induces a target automorphism b, i.e. that a pointed automorphism automatically preserves the tetragonal pencil. That inference is legitimate only when the residual pencil is COMPLETE: a preserves omega_C(-Gamma), but this yields b if and only if gamma is the morphism of the complete linear system |omega_C(-Gamma)|, which requires h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) = h^0(O_C(D)) = 2 exactly. On any fibre where h^0(O_C(D)) = 3, gamma^*H^0(P^1,O(1)) is a proper two-dimensional subpencil of a net, an automorphism preserving omega_C(-Gamma) need not preserve that subpencil, and the forgetful map degenerates precisely into the Aut(C,Gamma) versus Aut(C,gamma,Gamma) failure mode of FND-0137 — the clause would then be false as stated, not merely unproved. I attempted to produce such a point of Z. The attack is defeated because (i) the theorem hypothesizes fibrewise balanced F_s = O(4)+O(5) at EVERY point of S, not generically, and (ii) FND-0142 shows the only Clifford-equality route to h^0(D)=3 is a hyperelliptic-composed pencil, which FND-0125 computes to have relations bundle exactly F = O(2)+O(7), at splitting-type distance five from balanced. So the bad stratum is empty on S, and h^0(O_C(D)) = 2 holds identically. Had the artifact weakened balancedness to 'generically balanced', or dropped (N) (which is what forces L = omega_C(-D) by the deg A = 0 argument of FND-0105), this clause would be refuted rather than confirmed. Two lesser attacks were also run and did not survive as defects. First, coset-side typing: the statement indexes components by 'the left cosets H_alpha\S_6', but the orbits of left multiplication by H_alpha are the sets H_alpha g, which under standard naming are RIGHT cosets; the genuine left-coset set S_6/H_alpha carries no well-defined right multiplication, so on that reading the transitivity and stabilizer clauses would be ill-typed. The notation H_alpha\S_6 and the artifact's own stabilizer computation g^{-1}H_alpha g pin the correct reading, so this is a nomenclature slip (shared with the wording of FND-0148), not a mathematical error; recorded as FC-REV0150-COSET-SIDE. Second, global integrality of AJ_alpha is argued from local triviality alone, which gives only local integrality; the missing half-line (connected fibre bundle over a connected base, plus normality) is immediate. Nothing on the adversary checklist concerning cohomology degree versus Borel-Moore degree, Poincare duality and Tate twists, Gysin or Kunneth shifts, spectral-sequence differentials, semisimplification versus honest Hodge isomorphism, or predicted motives applies, because the artifact asserts no cohomological, weight, or Tate statement at all and says so explicitly (GAP-TATE). Likewise the stack-versus-coarse attack (FND-0144) and the ordered-versus-unordered integral-coefficient attack (FND-0075) find no purchase: the theorem is deliberately scheme-level and per-connected-component, disclaims any component or degree formula over a stack with inertia, and makes no descent to coarse moduli or to M_{6,6}. The one attack surface that the artifact leaves fully open is not a defect in the stated theorem but its scope: H_alpha is uncomputed, so the theorem is consistent with anything from 1 to 720 components, and it therefore supplies no input whatsoever to C66-TATE-SUPPORT. Confirming this lemma advances RED-0001 by exactly nothing, as the artifact itself states.
theorem_statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let S be a normal finite-type k-scheme carrying a smooth proper genus-six family pi:C->S, a P1-bundle P->S, and a finite flat degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl cover gamma:C->P satisfying (CE), fibrewise balanced relations F_s=O(4) direct-sum O(5), and the weak relative-canonical normalization (N). Let W_5 be the canonical degree-sixteen quotient in the balanced filtration, L=W_5 tensor omega_{C/S}^{-1}, B=Conf_6(C/S), and let Z be the intrinsic CE evaluation-failure subscheme of B. Let AJ be the relative projective plane representing effective divisors relatively linearly equivalent to L, and let U be its reduced-support open. Then Z is canonically the finite etale right S_6-torsor Ord(U)->U. For every connected component S_alpha of S, U_alpha=U times_S S_alpha is normal and integral. After choosing a geometric point u_alpha and an ordering above it, let H_alpha be the image of the monodromy homomorphism pi_1^et(U_alpha,u_alpha)->S_6. Then the irreducible components of Z_alpha=Z times_S S_alpha are indexed by the left cosets H_alpha\S_6. There are [S_6:H_alpha] such components; each maps finite etale and surjectively to U_alpha with degree |H_alpha|, has dimension dim(S_alpha)+2, and the right S_6-action is transitive on the component set with component stabilizer conjugate to H_alpha. In particular Z_alpha is irreducible if and only if H_alpha=S_6. Moreover, for every geometric point z=(C,gamma;x_1,...,x_6) of Z, the forgetful homomorphism from automorphisms of the tetragonal cover with movable target, namely pairs (a,b) satisfying a(x_i)=x_i and b composed with gamma=gamma composed with a, to Aut(C;x_1,...,x_6) is an isomorphism. Thus the ordered pointed-curve stabilizer is exactly the cover stabilizer in this explicitly defined sense.
